memory_update.text: Keep MP as the reference benchmark for U.S. integrated mine-to-magnet capacity, but avoid letting it crowd out smaller oxide/feedstock candidates.
Promote Energy Fuels to the underfollowed lane for deeper Layer 2 work because it is a U.S. NdPr oxide and monazite-processing node with potential heavy-rare-earth expansion.
Track Chemours as a hidden monazite/feedstock candidate; evidence is real but materiality needs verification in filings and contract volumes.
Track Critical Metals as a speculative shadow candidate for heavy rare-earth feedstock; survival depends on binding offtakes, project execution, financing and downstream qualification.

For rare_earth_magnet_compliance, prioritize companies that can prove non-Chinese feedstock provenance, oxide separation, heavy-rare-earth availability, magnet-maker qualification and defense/aerospace customer acceptance.
Layer 2 should verify actual commercial output and customer qualification for each candidate; nameplate capacity and offtake press releases are insufficient evidence for compliance-grade supply.

node: Compliant rare-earth magnets and qualified non-Chinese feedstock
summary: Layer 1B expansion focused on the scarce, policy-sensitive layer beneath headline rare-earth mining: qualified non-Chinese rare-earth oxides, heavy rare-earth feedstock, monazite supply, and magnet manufacturing capacity that can satisfy defense-origin and customer-certification requirements. The two-lane universe keeps MP Materials as the reference anchor, but the underfollowed lane points to Energy Fuels as a U.S. oxide/separation bottleneck, Chemours as a less obvious domestic monazite/feedstock supplier, and Critical Metals as a speculative heavy-rare-earth feedstock candidate tied to North American processors. No buy/sell view is implied.
